text:
incident-bot: HIGH SEV - spike in 5xx for Redwood API (us-east-1). Alerting on-call: @maya.k. auto-escalate after 5m if not acked.

maya.k: saw it, grabbing it now. numbers: ~12% 5xx over last 2m, p50 p95 latencies up ~3x for model-serving endpoints.

leo_sre: pinging — are GPUs healthy? any node restarts in the last hour?

maya.k: checking pod statuses + infra. quick grep: most 5xx show 502/504 from nginx-ingress -> downstream nvproxy. not seeing controller restarts.

priya-r: I can pull infra metrics. EBS ops show elevated latency on iops for some instances in eu-west? wait focusing us-east now. pulling /var/log/nvproxy* and kernel dmesg.

incident-bot: deploy-bot posted: canary-deploy/2026-03-15/rt-optimizations rolled 00:03:20 ago to us-east (10% traffic).

maya.k: uh — that canary just started before the spike. rolling it back to 0 now as precaution.

priya-r: rollback triggered by ops script: `kubectl set image deployment/model-serving model=/images/rt-optim:previous` — in progress.

ops-manager: thanks. also open a support case with AWS since we're seeing EC2 networking drops from Nitro on those host IDs. Dan, can you coordinate?

dan.partners: on it. I'm opening a Sev A with AWS. summary + logs coming. can someone paste host IDs and timestamps?

maya.k: host IDs: i-0abcde12345fgh678, i-0fedcba98765zy321. spikes started at 1935002420 unix ts. attaching sample nginx trace below.

maya.k: ```
[2026-03-15T14:07:03Z] "POST /v1/generate" 504 0.12s upstream: "10.20.5.13:8080" error: connect timeout
[2026-03-15T14:07:05Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 0.01s upstream: "10.20.5.14:8080" error: connection reset by peer
```

priya-r: adding VPC flow logs and ENI metrics. running: `aws ec2 create-flow-logs --resource-type NetworkInterface --resource-ids eni-0a1b2c3d4e5f --traffic-type ALL --log-group /aws/vpc/flow-logs` (example).

aws-support-bot: Support case created: #CASE-20260315-98765. AWS is assigning an engineer. Please provide ENI ids, instance IDs, and the flows you enabled.

dan.partners: copying case details to the vendor slack. AWS asked for packet captures — do we have rights to run tcpdump on those hosts?

leo_sre: we can capture on Node A (i-0abcde...) but need approval for any PII/data. captures will be limited to TCP headers; no payload.

ops-manager: approved for header-only captures for the case. Leo, Priya — take it.

leo_sre: starting capture: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 96 -w /tmp/ena-capture.pcap 'host 10.20.5.13 or host 10.20.5.14'`

maya.k: rollback completed at 1935002520. early signal: error rate dropped to ~6% and latency improving. still above baseline.

priya-r: ENI/EC2 metrics show brief RX drops at 14:06:35Z and 14:07:02Z aligning with 5xx spike. suspicious.

dan.partners: AWS engineer replied: "We've seen an upstream Nitro firmware jitter in this availability zone. We're investigating. Temporary mitigation: offload affected instances from service and move traffic to healthy AZ or warm spare hosts."

maya.k: initiating traffic shift for model-serving route policy to prefer us-east-2 and us-east-1b (if capacity allows). Applying routing policy change now.

priya-r: routing update command: `redwoodctl route update --service=model-serving --prefer-az us-east-2,us-east-1b --drain=60s` — applied.

incident-bot: status changed: mitigation underway — routing rebalanced.

ops-manager: drafting status page update. suggestion below, feel free to copy/edit: 

PR DRAFT (statuspage):
We are investigating elevated error rates and increased latencies affecting the Redwood API in the US-East region (partial impact to hosted inference endpoints). Engineers are actively rolling back a recent canary and shifting traffic to alternate availability zones while we coordinate with our cloud provider. Customers may see intermittent 5xx responses and higher latencies. We will post updates every 15 minutes.

maya.k: also prepared a customer notification (short-form):
Hi — We're investigating increased errors and latency affecting Redwood-hosted API in US-East. We have mitigations in place (rollback and traffic rerouting). No action required from customers; we’ll update here and via status.redwood.com. ETA for next update: 15 minutes.

ops-manager: add note for Dedicated customers: If you have private VPC attachments in us-east-1, you may see degraded performance. We'll reach out to account teams for high-commit customers.

dan.partners: AWS just messaged: "We've identified NIC firmware jitter on a subset of Nitro instances in us-east-1a. We're deploying a mitigation patch and can recommend instance replacement/stop-start or moving affected ENIs to healthy hosts. We'll update in 10 minutes."

leo_sre: for now we've drained 4 nodes out of the pool and are putting warm spares into service. error rate back to ~2% for most endpoints, still seeing rare spikes.

maya.k: preparing internal comms template for execs and CSMs:
Internal copy:
- Issue: Elevated 5xx and latency in us-east-1 starting 14:06 UTC. Root cause under investigation — upstream cloud NIC firmware jitter suspected.
- Impact: Partial impact to hosted API; some Dedicated customers on us-east attachments may see degraded performance.
- Mitigation: Rolled back canary, rerouted traffic to alternate AZ, drained affected nodes, AWS engaged (case #CASE-20260315-98765).
- Next steps: AWS mitigation patch verification, instance replacement plan, continuous monitoring.

ops-manager: nice. please include contact points: maya@redwood and dan@redwood for vendor comms.

aws-support-bot: AWS update: patch deployment started at 14:25 UTC. ETA for verification 20 minutes. Recommended: continue using warm spares and do instance replacement after patch.

maya.k: leaving a note for handoff — my on-call shift ends in 10m. Leo, can you take the pager and continue vendor coordination?

leo_sre: taking it. will stay with case until AWS confirms patch effectiveness and error rate stable for 30m.

maya.k: handing off: brief recap + links:
- Case #CASE-20260315-98765 (AWS)
- Flow logs: /aws/vpc/flow-logs/us-east-1/1935002468/
- Pcap: /tmp/ena-capture.pcap (sha256: d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e)
- Routing change ID: route-20260315-01
- Status page draft posted at 1935002620

leo_sre: ack. setting my status: `oncall (incidents)` and updating rotation. I'll post a confirmation once AWS verifies.

dan.partners: I've sent the CSMs a short note asking them to surface any high-impact customers. will coordinate account outreach if we need to send targeted notices.

ops-manager: good work team. keep updates in this thread. leaving a reminder to convert the short-form customer message into the formal support broadcast if we need to escalate.

incident-bot: update-schedule set: every 15m for 2h or until resolved.

aws-support-bot: AWS engineering: "Patch verification shows reduced error rates in affected hosts as of 14:40 UTC. Recommend replacement/stop-start of the affected EC2 instances to apply firmware fully."

leo_sre: scheduling instance replacements in a rolling fashion with 60s drain. plan: replace one node every 3 minutes to keep latency under SLOs. starting now.

maya.k: thanks — handing off completed. good luck. :rocket:

leo_sre: replacing nodes now. will update after 3 replacements or if error rate jumps.

ops-manager: once Leo confirms stable for 30m, publishing final status: "Service degraded — recovery complete" and notify customers that traffic shifted and instances replaced.

leo_sre: 1935003799 — after three replacements and 25 minutes of observation, 5xx rates back to baseline (<0.5%) and latency normalized. closing active mitigation.

dan.partners: updating case with AWS: "Patch validated, instances replaced, monitoring stable. closing on our side pending your confirmation."

incident-bot: incident status: resolved.

ops-manager: great job. make a short postmortem ticket and capture timeline + lessons (canary rollout timing, auto-rollback rules, vendor runbook). assigning to postmortems channel next.

maya.k: adding one immediate action item: tighten canary traffic ramp to 2m steady-state before pushing to 10% and add automatic rollback on 5xx>1% in 60s.

leo_sre: noted. creating a follow-up ticket with runbook edits and vendor comms template attached.

priya-r: saving logs and artifacts to S3:/incidents/1935002468/artifacts/ for postmortem.

ops-manager: thanks all.
